journal_options.note: ICMJE and Citing Medicine leave these three choices to the journal. The selected value is a profile option, not an NLM rule.

choices.range: (1-3) when the numbers are consecutive; otherwise comma-space between runs

multiple_citation.source: ICMJE g. References does not specify the separator. Citing Medicine chapters 1 and 2 state reference-list components, not in-text multi-number punctuation.

list_numbering.source: Neither ICMJE g. References nor NLM Sample References shows the list number. Citing Medicine examples are unnumbered component strings.

choices.unchanged: Leave the author's font, spacing, margins, and title page.

page_layout.source: ICMJE says to consult the journal's instructions. Citing Medicine chapters 1 and 2 do not set page layout.

authors.journal: Surname and at most two initials, no periods. First six, then et al. when more than six.
authors.journal_source: NLM Sample References #1: 'List the first six authors, followed by et al.' Citing Medicine Chapter 1, Author, General Rules, says to give all authors and points to Appendix F for MEDLINE. Appendix F is not in the chapter PDF. Chapter 1 example 3 shows the optional limit 'to 6 authors' as et al.
authors.book: Give all authors, regardless of the number.
authors.book_source: Citing Medicine Chapter 2A, Author/Editor, General Rules. Example 3 lists all. An optional limit to the first three is example 4, not the default.

title.case: Sentence case. Capitalize only the first word, proper nouns, proper adjectives, acronyms, and initialisms. Do not capitalize after a colon.
title.source: Citing Medicine Chapter 1, Article Title, General Rules; Chapter 2A, Title for Entire Books, General Rules

date.format: year, then a three-letter English month and the day when the typed entry has them (2004 May 5). End a journal date with a semicolon when a volume or issue follows.
date.source: Citing Medicine Chapter 1, Date of Publication for Journal Articles, General Rules. Book dates: Chapter 2A, Date of Publication (year required; month after the year only when present).

pages.format: Drop repeated leading digits and keep at least one digit of the end (123-125 becomes 123-5). Do not shorten when a letter follows the number (124A-126A). Keep a leading letter (S10-8). Keep roman numerals as found. Shorten each span of a discontinuous list on its own.
pages.source: Citing Medicine Chapter 1, Location (Pagination), General Rules and examples 59-61. The same shortening is in Chapter 2C, Location (Pagination) of the Part of a Book.

references.medline_attested_note: MEDLINE abbreviations from the PubMed source field, stored with the sample and not looked up at format time: N Engl J Med (PMID 12140307), Brain Res (PMID 12062471), BMJ (PMID 19129307). Any other journal title is left as typed unless the user supplies the abbreviation.
